messages:
Maria: Heads-up from last night: P99 latency jump caused some 500s for a slice of customers. The pager landed fine but the post-incident write-up got scattered across threads. We should tighten handoff -> postmortem creation.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-043 created via paging: latency spike. Severity: Sev2. Notifying @oncall-rotation. Channel archived to #incidents/2026/043.
Alejandro: Quick timeline for context: 22:58 pager, 23:03 scaled service pool, 23:26 pinned fallback model. Impact window ~22:58-23:18 for affected orgs. A small percent of requests errored with 500s.
Sam: I missed the initial page (was mid-deploy), handed over at 23:10. Rachel picked up triage while I stabilized pods.
Rachel: Can we make it so the postmortem has a canonical owner and timeline? Right now it's in the pager log + this channel + a couple of DMs. Hard to track.
Maria: Proposal: have IncidentBot create a draft postmortem doc automatically when Sev2+ incidents close, pre-filled with timeline, mitigations, and a participant list. That reduces copy/paste.
Devon: Agree in principle. Need an opt-out — some noisy incidents shouldn't spawn docs. Suggest flags like `/incident finalize --pm` or `--no-pm`.
Alejandro: Could the bot populate a short template: title, 2-line summary, impact section listing orgs, timeline from pager, and owners? If we auto-tag participants that saves a lot.
Maria: Example draft structure I want auto-generated (compact):
```
Title: [AUTO] INC-2026-043 latency excursion
Summary: 1-2 lines
Impact: org IDs, duration, error types
Timeline: auto-sourced from pager + channel
Participants: @alice @bob @oncall-rotation
Action items: placeholder block
```
Sam: Also add an owner assignment step. If no owner claimed within 48h, ping the SRE lead and push a low-priority follow-up into the remediation board.
Rachel: Privacy note: auto drafts should default to private (draft) until the owner sets visibility. Some threads reference customer identifiers that need redaction.
Devon: Dashboard fields we should capture: severity, root-cause hypothesis, indicators (metrics), estimated cost impact, model version, and a link to any downstream ticket. Makes it searchable for regressions.
Maria: UX idea: `/pm create-from-incident INC-2026-043 --template=triage` opens a modal to select owner, set visibility, and attach extra traces.
Alejandro: Integrations-wise, postmortems must be first-class objects in the remediation DB (not just docs). That lets us query by tag, model-version, or customer.
ops-bot: Reminder: oncall rotation updated. Use `/oncall who` to confirm next week.
Sam: Can we trial this for two weeks? Start with Sev1-2 only, monitor noise. If false-positives heavy, expand opt-out patterns.
Rachel: Our incident export currently grabs pager logs but not runtime trace annotations (like KV cache metrics). We'll need a helper to pull runtime traces into the draft or attach a trace link.
Maria: Proposed rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (1 week experiment): IncidentBot auto-creates a private draft for Sev2+ incidents when the incident is closed. Draft includes timeline, mitigation steps, and participant tags. Add `/pm claim <INC>` to claim ownership. 48h reminder if unclaimed.
- Phase 2 (3 weeks): Add remediation dashboard integration: auto-create row items from action templates, allow `create-jira` from the draft. Capture key metadata for searching.
- Phase 3 (Q2): Modal templates, trace attachments (runtime/trace links), visibility controls, and aggregation dashboards for regression trends.
Devon: Tech notes: IncidentBot needs a service account with doc write permissions and limited Jira scopes. We'll route this through the integrations service and file an RFC for security.
Maria: I'll start an RFC + draft schema for the postmortem object. Volunteers: Alejandro for bot changes, Devon for dashboard parsing, Sam for reminders and owner flows, Rachel for trace ingestion/privacy.
Alejandro: I'll prototype the bot endpoint and template generator today and open a PR.
Sam: I'll own the claim/48h reminder logic and the flag to escalate to SRE lead.
Rachel: I'll map trace sources and the redaction checklist; will post the privacy checklist by Wednesday.
Devon: I'll sketch the remediation board schema and the parser for action-item lines so the dashboard can turn them into tasks.
incident-bot: Note: experimental flag `pm-autogen` available. Use `incident-bot toggle pm-autogen --staging` to enable in staging.
Maria: One UX rule: auto-populated sections should be prefixed with `[AUTO]` so reviewers can tell what was machine-sourced vs human-written.
Alejandro: PR: https://git.redwood/repo/incident-bot/pull/197 (WIP)
Sam: If you need test orgs or synthetic incidents to exercise the flow, ping me and I'll create them.
Maria: Timeline ask: can we get Phase 1 live as an experiment by next Thursday? If there are blockers, call them out here so we can re-prioritize.
Rachel: I'll validate privacy constraints before the draft is shared outside the claim-owner.
Devon: I'll prepare the minimal dashboard ingestor to translate action-item patterned lines like `- [ ] owner — description — due YYYY-MM-DD — tags: [infra]` into rows.
Maria: Great. I'll post the RFC to #eng-oncall and #eng-sre shortly and include acceptance criteria. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
